plan: [ This is effectively a second‑price (Vickrey) auction: final price equals the second‑highest sealed bid. With independent private values and risk neutrality, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. Underbidding risks losing profitably when the clock is below my value; overbidding risks winning at a price above my value if a rival’s bid lies between my value and my inflated bid. [ With independent private values and a second-price outcome (winner pays the second-highest sealed bid), the weakly dominant strategy is to bid my true value. This maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies: I win exactly when it’s profitable (when others’ bids are below my value) and pay the second-highest bid. Overbidding risks paying above value; underbidding risks losing profitable cases near my value. With no past-history to exploit and one round only, bid equals 34. ]

This is a second-price auction via an ascending clock: the winner pays the second-highest sealed bid. The dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Truthful bidding wins whenever my value is highest and pays at most the second-highest value. Overbidding risks negative profit; underbidding sacrifices positive surplus. I will bid 10.
